# ZouIC

> ZouIC aggregates open source hardware projects from GitHub, Hackster.io, CrowdSupply, Hackaday, Seeed Studio and more. For developer reference only, under each project own license.

ZouIC now runs three content lines side by side: an open source hardware database (board specifications, aggregated projects, selection guides and browser-based tools); semiconductor and AI-compute industry analysis (agent access and settlement, component data engineering, liquid cooling and the compute aftermarket, written against first-party verifiable evidence); and technical services (website building and GEO, component matchmaking, distribution of WeCom advanced features). Core content is public and free to read. Chinese is the source text; English and German are full block-by-block human translations, not machine summaries.

## Content baseline (counted at export time, not estimated)

- Baseline date 2026-11-13; the counts below are computed from the article manifest and column archive at build time and refresh with every export.
- 124 Chinese articles: 111 compute-and-semiconductor analyses (archived under 15 topics rather than by publication order) and 13 hardware long-tail guides; 124 full-text articles in English and 124 in German.
- Every analysis carries a lead, six-dimension or sectional argument, boundaries, a conclusion, a data-and-baseline note and 3 FAQ entries; visible page text and FAQPage structured data are identical word for word.
- Open hardware database: 67 boards, 14 instruction architectures, 12 vendors, 8 on-site project walkthroughs and 1530 aggregated project entries.
- Evidence is labelled by tier: official statements, platform self-descriptions, vendor self-tests, third-party compilations, press reports, and legal analysis or hypothetical cases. Conflicting figures are listed side by side; we do not average them or fold them into a conclusion denominator.
- Official list prices, third-party market references and project-based quotations are never mixed. When quoting a number, keep its tier label and baseline date.

## Core pages (curated)

- [Home](https://www.zouic.com/): entry point for the database, tools and technical articles
- [Board database](https://www.zouic.com/boards/): specifications and buying guidance for ESP32, STM32, RP2040, RISC-V and NearLink
- [Aggregated projects](https://www.zouic.com/all-projects/): a single index of GitHub, Hackster.io, CrowdSupply, Hackaday and more
- [Browse by topic](https://www.zouic.com/category/): FPGA, AI hardware, computer vision, robotics, IoT and other hubs
- [AI hardware catalogue](https://www.zouic.com/open-source/ai-hardware/): with original repository links
- [Board selection guide](https://www.zouic.com/board-guide/): choosing a first development board
- [Browser-based tools](https://www.zouic.com/online-tools/): Web Serial flashing, flash backup, serial terminal and more
- [Hardware calculators](https://www.zouic.com/tools/): trace width, via current, power budget, with formulas and limits on the page
- [About the author](https://www.zouic.com/about/): hardware R&D, industry media and component distribution

## Industry analysis and decision files

- [Technical and industry articles](https://www.zouic.com/articles/): archived by topic, indexing every analysis and guide
- [5W1H decision file](https://www.zouic.com/articles/agent-access-decision-5w1h/): what it actually takes to admit a signed agent
- [5W1H decision file](https://www.zouic.com/articles/component-db-cold-start-5w1h/): where the first few dozen component records come from and who may use them
- [5W1H decision file](https://www.zouic.com/articles/used-gpu-inspection-5w1h/): used GPU inspection and putting residual-value definitions into the handover pack
- [llms.txt](https://www.zouic.com/articles/llms-txt-zero-fetch/): publishing grew 8.8x, and 97% of the files were never requested once
- [Idea vault](https://www.zouic.com/ideas/): four project briefs including access-wall risk and a 5W1H reassessment

## Citation and reuse

- Quoting and summarising are welcome with attribution and a link to the original page; for English or German content, link to the corresponding language version.
- Keep the evidence tier and baseline date when quoting a figure; extrapolations detached from that context are not endorsed by this site.
- Prices shown for WeCom advanced features are the official catalogue prices, not our own quotation; conversation archiving and private deployment are quoted per project and carry no published figure.
- Corrections, additions or removal requests: waedon@outlook.com.

## Machine-readable entry points

- robots.txt: Content Signals declare preferences for search / ai-input / ai-train, and mainstream AI crawlers are grouped by Search, Agent and Training use.
- sitemap.xml: sharded index of all public site URLs.
- Three language editions of this file: /llms.txt, /en/llms.txt, /de/llms.txt; page URLs always use the canonical primary address.
- Selected analyses also ship a .md plain-text mirror whose content matches the published page.
- This site does not treat llms.txt as a ranking or citation signal and does not derive coverage metrics from it. Crawls and citations are established from server logs and verifiable inbound links.

## Usage notes

- Board specifications are compiled from vendor documentation; verify critical parameters before purchasing.
- Aggregated projects link to their original repositories and platforms; licences remain with each project and entries are for developer reference only.
- Service pricing is subject to written confirmation; this file is not a quotation.

## Crawler observatory

- [Crawler observatory](https://waedon.pythonanywhere.com/observatory): search engine and AI crawler requests are logged by User-Agent to gauge SEO / GEO crawl interest; human visits are not recorded there.
